entry.title: About me, and about this blog
entry.summary: Who I am, an R&D engineer in control and embedded AI heading into a CIFRE PhD with Stellantis and IMS, and what this blog will cover.
entry.content:
I'm Elias Charbel Salameh, an R&D engineer at ADERA in Bordeaux. I work on mixed AI / model-based approaches for low-consumption, certifiable embedded automotive algorithms. It is the same research project as my upcoming CIFRE PhD with Stellantis and the IMS laboratory, started ahead of time.

Where I'm coming from

  • Education. A B.E. in Electrical & Electronics Engineering at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), then a double-degree M.Sc. in Complex Systems Engineering (Automation & Robotics of Intelligent Systems) at the Université de Technologie de Compiègne (UTC).
  • Control under uncertainty. As an R&D intern at the OpenLab Stellantis–IMS–SANPSY, I worked on Adaptive Cruise Control for connected automated vehicles: robust MPC, soft-constrained MPC and reinforcement learning, benchmarked across speed profiles, and a Safe-RL controller with Control Barrier Functions.
  • Robotics. My final-year project at USEK studied a SLAM pipeline for the Unitree AlienGo quadruped, fusing a 3D LiDAR, an IMU and an Intel RealSense D435i depth camera.
  • Computer vision. At inmind.ai academy I built an end-to-end object-detection pipeline for BMW assembly-line items with YOLOv5 (98.4% mAP).
  • Teaching and community. I lead lab sessions on linear systems dynamics at the Université de Bordeaux, and I was Head of Judges for the World Robot Olympiad Lebanon 2025, coordinating 42 judges.

The portfolio has every entry in detail, and its timeline can be filtered by topic: for example the entries that use MPC or the research work.

What this blog is for

Posts here will follow the same threads as that timeline: control, robotics and embedded AI, and the projects and teaching around them.
